summary: ECOWAS citizens enter Côte d'Ivoire freely, while most other visitors pre-enroll online for the biometric eVisa (about EUR 73) and collect it on arrival at Abidjan airport — arrivals by land or through other airports need an embassy visa, and a yellow fever certificate is required from everyone.

payments.text: Cards are accepted at hotels, supermarkets and better restaurants in Abidjan, but cash and mobile money (Wave, Orange Money, MTN) dominate everywhere else. Carry CFA francs outside the big cities.

safety.text: Abidjan, Yamoussoukro and the coast are generally welcoming, with pickpocketing and bag-snatching the main urban risks. The far north along the Mali and Burkina Faso borders carries a terrorism risk. Check advisories before overland trips there.

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to March is the driest stretch on the coast — good for Abidjan, Grand-Bassam and Assinie; May to July brings the heaviest rain in the south.

tips.text: The eVisa is only issued on arrival at Abidjan airport — if you enter by land or through another airport, you need a visa from an embassy before travel.
Yellow fever certificates are checked systematically at Abidjan airport, before immigration. Keep the yellow card with your passport.
Avoid the northern border zones with Mali and Burkina Faso, including the northern fringe of Comoé National Park — jihadist groups have carried out attacks there.
Mobile money is everywhere — Wave and Orange Money QR codes work for taxis, maquis restaurants and market stalls where cards never will.
Pre-enroll only through the official SNEDAI service — unofficial eVisa sites charge heavy mark-ups and cannot speed up the airport counter.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Côte d'Ivoire?
faq.answer: ECOWAS citizens enter freely without a visa. Almost everyone else needs one — for arrivals at Abidjan airport, pre-enroll online for the eVisa (about EUR 73) and collect the biometric visa at the dedicated counter on landing; for land borders or other airports, obtain a visa from an Ivorian embassy first.

faq.question: How does the Côte d'Ivoire eVisa work?
faq.answer: You pre-enroll and pay online through the official SNEDAI service, upload your details, and receive a pre-enrollment approval by email within a few business days. On arrival at Abidjan Félix-Houphouët-Boigny Airport you go to the eVisa counter before immigration, where your biometrics are taken and the visa is placed in your passport.

faq.question: Can I use the eVisa at a land border?
faq.answer: No. The pre-enrolled eVisa is issued only at Abidjan airport. Travelers entering from Ghana, Liberia, Guinea, Mali or Burkina Faso by land need a visa from an embassy before traveling.

faq.question: Is the yellow fever vaccine mandatory for Côte d'Ivoire?
faq.answer: Yes. A yellow fever certificate is required from all travelers aged 9 months and over, whatever country you arrive from, and it is checked on arrival.

faq.question: Is Côte d'Ivoire safe to visit?
faq.answer: Abidjan, the coast and the central regions are generally fine for travelers who take normal big-city precautions. The far north along the Mali and Burkina Faso borders carries a real terrorism risk and is best avoided. Check current advisories before overland travel.
